An Apple billboard showing a young child holding an iPhone has sparked criticism in Italy, prompting the country's child rights watchdog to refer the ad to three regulatory bodies. Here's what happened.

Apple's 'Relax, it's iPhone' ad campaign causes controversy in Italy

Italy's Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA) has raised concerns over an Apple billboard in Milan showing a young child holding an iPhone, accompanied by the slogan 'Tutto ok, è iPhone'.

The ad is part of Apple's long-running 'Relax, it's iPhone' campaign, which typically showcases iPhones surviving various potentially damaging scenarios.

The latest billboards in the series show iPhones being used in heavy rain, knocked off tables by cats, and carried in dogs' mouths.

One new billboard in the series shows a young child holding an iPhone — seemingly meant to reassure parents that even if a child drops the phone, it will be fine. But the ad has sparked backlash, with AGIA calling it part of a normalisation of "infantilising electronic devices".

In a press release, AGIA said its attention was drawn to the ad by a Milan resident, who said the image was "disturbing" because it "brings together two worlds that should remain separate".

AGIA said it has referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the country's competition authority AGCM, and the advertising industry's self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate examination and any possible action".

Apple has yet to publicly respond to the controversy.
